newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Caltex says to cut Singapore staff by 15 percent.
newsitem.headline: Caltex says to cut Singapore staff by 15 percent.

text.p: Caltex Petroleum Corp, a joint venture company owned equally by Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp, said on Wednesday it was cutting about 15 percent of its Singapore staff.

The company said it has completed a restructuring, which will include reducing Singapore staff by 50. Compensation, help in searching for another job and counselling will be provided to those affected, the company said.
A spokesman for Caltex said the job cuts did not reflect any change in the company's view of Singapore. He said the city-state remained Caltex global hub.
He added that it was unlikely any traders would be affected by the cuts. Generally, the cuts would be made in administration, he said.
The changes include positioning Jock McKenzie in Singapore as vice-president in charge of Southeast Asia and Richard Fernie as vice-president in charge of Middle East, Africa and South Asia.

Last September Caltex chairman David Law-Smith said a reorganisation was to take place in order to make Caltex "more agile and clearly to be in a position to execute strategies within a very prompt time frame."
He said positioning the vice-presidents in Singapore would speed up decision making, which would otherwise be made at the company's corporate office in Irving, Texas.
